dimensional_audit.mathematical_implication: Direct transfer of internal hidden activations fails because LLaMA/Mistral (dim=4096) and Qwen (dim=1536) span incompatible vector spaces. Feeding Qwen activations into a detector trained on LLaMA/Mistral requires an arbitrary projection matrix W in R^(1536 x 4096), introducing uncalibrated projection distortion.
dimensional_audit.behavioral_feature_contrast: By contrast, logit-derived behavioral statistics (output entropy, logit gap, top-5 probability mass, top-1 probability, distribution spread, and logprob mean) yield an identical 6-dimensional summary per probe regardless of hidden dimension, preserving cross-family structural compatibility.

internal_activations.memory_overhead: High (~14-16 GB VRAM needed to retain intermediate tensor activations in fp16)
internal_activations.quantization_support: Poor. In quantized GGUF engines (llama.cpp), intermediate activations are dequantized ephemerally and discarded to minimize memory.
internal_activations.hook_latency: High (requires memory copies per layer across 28-32 transformer blocks)
internal_activations.portability: Tied to specific model architecture definition and tensor names

behavioral_fingerprints.memory_overhead: Negligible (only requires top-K logits of final output token, < 100 KB)
behavioral_fingerprints.quantization_support: Native. Runs identically on 4-bit, 8-bit, or 16-bit GGUF/AWQ/GPTQ models.
behavioral_fingerprints.hook_latency: Zero hook overhead (evaluated directly on returned logits)
behavioral_fingerprints.cross_architecture_compatibility: Universal (fixed 180 dimensions across all LLM families)
behavioral_fingerprints.portability: High. Black-box queryable via standard API endpoints

scientific_conclusion: Internal model representations are non-invariant across architectures due to differing hidden dimensions (4096 vs 1536) and layer topologies (32 vs 28 layers). Furthermore, intermediate activation extraction incurs prohibitive memory overhead (14-16 GB VRAM) and is poorly supported in quantized GGUF runtimes. Output logit-derived behavioral features remain the only representation that is universally dimension-compatible and black-box queryable across arbitrary model families.
